data.title: Arab Parliament: Repeated Houthi Attacks on Saudi Civilian Facilities Constitute Systematic Terrorism
data.content:
Cairo, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Arab Parliament condemned in the strongest terms the continued terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia on civilian facilities and property in Riyadh, which caused material damage to a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD).
    It stressed that deliberately targeting vital facilities and endangering civilian lives and property constitutes a flagrant violation of international law and international humanitarian law and demonstrates a serious disregard for their provisions.
    In a statement issued today, the Arab Parliament said the militia's continued reliance on violence and terrorism, targeting the security of countries and their peoples' resources, requires taking deterrent international measures to prevent the continuation of these practices, hold those responsible accountable, and prevent them from escaping punishment.
    The Arab Parliament urged the United Nations, the UN Security Council, countries worldwide, and regional and international organizations to take decisive action against the Houthi militia. It called for the militia to be designated a terrorist organization, its activities criminalized, and its funding sources pursued. Such measures would help cut off funding for terrorism and limit the militia's ability to carry out further attacks and threaten regional security and stability.
    The Arab Parliament reaffirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for all measures taken by the Kingdom to protect its security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity. It stressed that Saudi Arabia's security is a red line and an integral part of Arab national security, and that any threat to it poses a direct danger to regional security and stability.
    -- SPA
